gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on every row via a temporary vitest test (scripts/.tmp-checkgate.test.ts, not pushed — deleted before commit) against the full draft set, using the real allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt. First-draft level drift (9 of 16 rows flagged on the first pass — background words that are not on the allow-list and were introduced while drafting: palace · thousands · queen · saturday · england · wales · picnic · helmet · cyclist · harbour · awake · soup · chef · dull · pasta · spicy · delicious · grill · beans; plus one structural failure, "round" item 1 written with two blank markers instead of one) were fixed with allow-listed replacements (each checked individually with grep -x before reuse) and a single-blank rewrite, then re-verified to 16/16. A negative control (7 extra rows, each broken on one distinct axis — Latin letters in translation_he, nikud in translation_he, headword missing from its own example, an item stem over the word limit, a stem with no blank marker, a stem that leaks the target word in its own body, two near_synonym distractors leaving fewer than 4 scorable) was run through the same real gate immediately after the real 16/16 pass and correctly rejected on all 7 (0/7 passed) before any row was trusted. A separate grammar read-through after the gate pass caught one row ("ruin", item 2) where the bare verb form did not agree with its sentence context ("he almost ruin the trip") — the gate does not check subject-verb agreement — and it was rewritten ("he was about to ruin the trip") and re-verified.
distractor_allowed_words_note: Distractor words were checked by hand against allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt after drafting (grep -x on all 53 distinct distractor words used): 30 confirmed present, 23 not present — bacon · banana · burger · carrot · expressive · gravy · hockey · jogging · junction · loyal · massage · noble · pencil · pepper · pillow · roundworm · rugged · runway · safari · sailor · salad · spoil · umbrella · unhappily. This is the same open, unresolved gap recorded in every manifest since 12-13/09 (C-0545 onward): gateSense does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all, and the words used here are the same class of simple, universally-known basic nouns/adjectives already reused as 'unrelated'/'orthographic' distractors across many prior batches (pencil, umbrella, banana, carrot, guitar all recur in earlier manifests) — not a new problem introduced by this tick.
he_one_to_many_note: Every planned translation_he was grepped against every existing translation_he in the bank before finalising. Four genuine collisions were found and resolved: "progressive"→"מתקדם" collides with "advanced" (batch-2026-09-11.jsonl) — tagged he_one_to_many_group "מתקדם = advanced/progressive" rather than invented a less accurate word. "ruin"→"להרוס" collides with "destroy" (batch-2026-08-29-4.jsonl) — tagged "להרוס = destroy/ruin". "safe"→"בטוח" collides with both "sure" (batch-2026-08-13.jsonl) and "certain" (batch-2026-08-29-2.jsonl) — a genuine Hebrew one-to-many (בטוח covers both the safety sense and the confidence sense), tagged "בטוח = safe/sure/certain". "sake"→"טובה" collides with "favor" (batch-2026-09-13-3.jsonl) — tagged "טובה = favor/sake". A fifth near-collision was avoided rather than tagged: "sailing" was drafted first as "שייט" (the generic word for boating/cruising), which collides with "cruise" (batch-2026-09-13-2.jsonl) but is not a true one-to-many — cruise and sailing are distinct concepts (a large-ship trip vs. the sport of a boat under sail) that a shared loose translation was blurring, so "sailing" was retranslated to the more precise "הפלגה" instead of tagging a false collision. The other 11 headwords (round · roundabout · royal · rugby · runner · running · rush · sadly · salt · sauce · sausage) were each grepped individually and confirmed to have no untagged collision.
translation_confidence_note: 1 of 16 rows is translation_confidence:"low": "round" (the adverb sense, as in 'turn round') — Hebrew has no single clean one-word equivalent for this specific adverbial sense distinct from 'around', and a learner is likely to conflate round (adverb, direction-change) with round (adjective, circular shape); this is recorded as its own he_interference_note rather than omitted (STEP 5: never omit a word for uncertainty). 2 of 16 rows are "medium": "rush" ("בהילות" is accurate but slightly more formal/literary than the everyday English word) and "sake" (the 'for the sake of' idiom does not map onto a single Hebrew noun 1:1 — see the one-to-many note above). The remaining 13 rows are "high".
batch_size_note: 16 rows, one sense each, full apparatus (2 examples, 3 leveled items, 4 tagged distractors) per row.
